item.title: The Weedy Garden
item.description: In The Weedy Garden, readers gain an intimacy with nature that is easy to miss when standing at adult height.

item.title: The Sun and the Starmaker
item.description: The love in The Sun and the Starmaker is mature and goes beyond happily ever after to show how even in the darkest of times, love can prevail.

item.title: This Is the Door
item.description: Darcey Steinke’s lucid, kaleidoscopic This Is the Door illuminates pain as a transformative power that brings us closer to life’s fragility and wonder.

item.title: The World of Black Film
item.description: Thanks to author Ashley Clark’s expertise, The World of Black Film will introduce even the best-read cinephiles to works they hadn’t heard of before.

item.title: Why Fly
item.description: With her aviation memoir, Why Fly, Caroline Paul reminds us that adventure stories have an uncanny ability to bring us closer to each other as we stand closer to the edge.

item.title: 4 remarkable nonfiction books that shed light on human behavior
item.description: Jane Borden’s fascinating Cults Like Us explores why Americans are receptive to doomsday thinking, plus more great history books perfect for book clubs.

item.title: Caroline Paul’s ‘Why Fly’ is “a meditation on the way flight can expand a life”
item.description: Piloting a tiny, experimental gyrocopter helped Paul find her footing as her marriage ended.

item.title: Getting into the weeds with Margaret and Billy Renkl
item.description: The sibling duo and creators of cherished adult nonfiction about the natural world discuss their first picture book together.

item.title: “There are so many ways a cave can kill you”
item.description: A caving expedition descends into chaos in Taylor Adams’ latest suspense novel, Her Last Breath.

item.title: 3 YA fantasy books to watch out for
item.description: Need a respite from reality? Let these three imaginative young adult novels whisk you away to new, thrilling worlds.
